sources.label: This site, build 1.60.1.70009's engine fork (sim/core target auto-attack, attack table and TMI)
Blizzard, Deep Dive panel recap (the Phase 1 raid is the level 60 content the beta does not yet reach)

notes: The one statement of the fight every tank spec is simmed against: what a tank's BiS rows, stat weights and headline figures (effective health, damage taken per second, chance of death, threat per second) are measured on. Nothing public states a Forever raid boss's melee numbers (the beta stops at level 30 and no Phase 1 boss has been datamined), so this is a stand-in, built so every figure is a RELATIVE comparison between sets and none is a prediction of a named boss; the reasons below say what each number stands for and what would change it. The boss is the target the character already fights (level 63 at 60: api.DefaultTargetLevel), tanked by the character, hitting with one melee swing; crushing blows and critical hits come from the engine's own attack table for the three-level gap, not from a number here. The tank carries the Phase 1 raid buffs and tank consumables of data/curated/presets.json's raid preset when ranked raid-ready, and the class kit alone when ranked bare. Bands below 60 fight the same boss with its damage and the healers' output scaled by character level over 60, a stand-in for dungeon bosses at that level.

level_scaling.reason: Damage and healing scale linearly with character level over the reference level, so a level 40 tank faces a boss in the same proportion to its own health as a level 60 tank faces the raid boss. A dungeon boss table would replace this; none is published.

swing_speed_sec.reason: One melee swing every 2.0 seconds, the cadence of most Classic raid melee bosses. A faster boss favours block value and avoidance streaks less than a slower, harder-hitting one; 2.0 s sits between.

min_base_damage.reason: The least a swing rolls before armor at the reference level. The engine rolls the minimum up to (1 + damage spread) times it, so the mean unmitigated swing is about 2,900 at level 60. Chosen so a raid-ready level 60 tank takes a few hundred damage per second and is rarely killed, while a bare one is killed in a real share of fights: the range in which armor, avoidance and health all move the result.

damage_spread.reason: The engine's own enemy swing rule (sim/core/attack.go EnemyWeaponDamage): a swing rolls between the minimum and 133% of it, so the spread is 0.33. Kept as the engine states it.

parry_haste.reason: A parried swing advances the boss's next swing, as in Classic. It makes parry worth less than the avoided damage alone suggests, which the weights should show.

dual_wield.reason: A single melee swing. Raid bosses that dual wield are rare and would only double the table the tank rolls against.

hps.reason: Healing per second the tank receives at level 60, the output of the healers the raid assigns to the main tank. The healers are assumed, not simulated: they heal in a steady cadence regardless of the tank's health, so chance of death measures how often the tank's health runs out between heals and total damage taken cannot be undone by a fast heal. Set so that a poorly mitigated set dies in a real share of fights, because the healers cannot catch up with its spikes, and a well mitigated one rarely does.

cadence_sec.reason: The healers' median time between heals on the tank, the engine's default when unset.

cadence_variation_sec.reason: How far each heal lands from the median cadence. Real healing arrives unevenly; a variation of a quarter of the cadence keeps the chance-of-death figure from depending on one lucky run of heals.

burst_window_sec.reason: The TMI window. The engine's published TMI is the log-sum of damage in sliding windows of this length as a share of the tank's health, the standard 6 seconds, so spiky incoming damage is penalised the way a healer's reaction time would punish it.
